title: Funan and Oc Eo
summary: Funan is the earliest known kingdom of the Khmer area, flourishing from around the first to the sixth century AD according to the Library of Congress; EBSCO says Chenla annexed it in 627. Its first capital was Vyadhapura, later Angkor Borei, and its port city Oc Eo lay about 55 miles south of Angkor Borei, with a canal network over 120 miles long.

uncertainty.note: LoC: around the first to the sixth century A.D. EBSCO: 1st century to c. 627 C.E., when Chenla annexed Funan.

as_recorded.value: flourished from around the first to the sixth century A.D.

where.modern_name: Oc Eo, An Giang Province, Mekong Delta, Vietnam (Angkor Borei, Cambodia, was the later capital)
where.historical_name: Oc Eo, port city of Funan (name recorded by Chinese chroniclers)

importance.justification: Earliest known kingdom in the Cambodia and Mekong Delta area, with a major port at Oc Eo.

sources.title: Cambodia: A Country Study, Historical Setting
sources.publisher: Library of Congress Federal Research Division

reviewer_note: Point is Oc Eo; the kingdom was larger and its capital sites are uncertain (60 km uncertainty, Angkor Borei is the later capital per EBSCO). Dates are century-level and differ slightly by source.
